findings.issue: When a viewer texture is disposed, its GL objects stay allocated until another converter runs. These are the RGBA output texture, the plane textures, the shaders and every cached dma-buf texture. The cached textures keep the decoder's dma-buf surfaces alive, because each one is a sibling of an EGLImage. In an app that sits in the tray after one session, this GPU memory (shared RAM on an iGPU) is held until the user opens another viewer.
findings.evidence: ~VideoGl (lines 394-409) calls eglDestroyImageKHR and only queues the GL names into g_textures, g_framebuffers, g_buffers and g_programs. Collect(), which deletes them, is called in one place only: VideoGl::Convert, line 718. Nothing runs it from Texture(), finalize or dispose. Per EGL_KHR_image_base, a texture made from an EGLImage keeps its storage after eglDestroyImageKHR, so up to kMaxImages = 24 imported planes (12 decoder surfaces) stay referenced. finalize in desktop_video.cc resets the converter on the GTK thread with no context current.
findings.fix: Free the names in Flutter's share group when the texture goes. One way: at the first Convert, create a small private EGL context that shares with eglGetCurrentContext(), using the current context's EGL_CONFIG_ID or EGL_KHR_no_config_context. ~VideoGl then makes that context current surfaceless on its own thread, waits on or destroys the in-flight fences, deletes the textures, framebuffers, buffer and programs directly, and releases the context. Keep the global queue only as a fallback.

findings.issue: populate acquires the picture, which sends Rust its 'presented' receipt, before converting it. If Convert fails, the picture is never shown but still counts as presented. Rust's recovery relies on presentations: 'units handed out with nothing presented for 700 ms' ask for an IDR, and 'five decoder errors in 30 s with nothing presented' end the session as decoder_failed. A persistent GL failure (shader or FBO setup, upload error, a size beyond the GL limits) therefore leaves a black or frozen viewer that Rust believes is presenting, with no IDR request and no fallback. The dma-buf refusal case also receipts every dma-buf picture published before the decoder thread rebuilds the pipeline, none of which is shown.
findings.evidence: desktop_video.cc:346 calls module->acquire, whose first acquisition calls api_.presented (desktop_video_gst.cc, PbVideoDecoder::Acquire). Convert runs afterwards at :359, and on failure the picture is released and Texture() returns the previous picture or the black pixel. docs/remote-desktop.md:994 says the consumer reports each frame it actually showed. Before this change, copy_pixels had no failure path.
findings.fix: ABI 2 is new in this PR, so split the receipt from the acquisition: `acquire` returns the picture unreceipted, and a new `present(decoder, picture)` sends the receipt after Convert succeeds. Also, after N consecutive conversion failures on system-memory pictures, have the module report `failed`, so Rust's decoder_failed and JPEG fallback apply.

findings.issue: The doc says a system-memory picture 'goes back to the decoder as soon as the upload returns'. The code keeps it out of the pool until the next picture is converted, and the same paragraph's allocation sentence says the one on screen stays out.
findings.evidence: desktop_video.cc populate: after a successful Convert it sets `previous = state->shown; state->shown = next;` and releases only `previous`. The just-uploaded picture stays retained as `shown`, which Snapshot later retains again for GStreamer's converter.
findings.fix: Reword it, for example: 'the picture stays out of the decoder's pool while it is on screen, so that a snapshot can convert it'. Alternatively, release system-memory pictures right after the upload and take the snapshot from the GPU still, as for dma-bufs.

findings.issue: The CHANGELOG and both user guides state the dma-buf path as fact: VA-API pictures on GStreamer 1.24 are 'sampled where the decoder wrote them, with no copy to system memory at all' and 'stay in GPU memory'. Nothing has run that path, not CI and not a device. The code also falls back to system memory for good whenever the negotiated modifier cannot be imported as single-plane R8/GR88 (Mesa rejects CCS/DCC modifiers whose plane count is above 1). The brief asked for a CHANGELOG bullet with device figures; none exist, which is honest, but the effect claims are unverified.
findings.evidence: The implementer's report lists 'the whole dma-buf path, which no CI job can exercise' as device-only. docs/remote-desktop.md:2389-2392 itself says the dma-buf path 'has not run'. CHANGELOG.md:7, docs/user-guide.md:415 and docs/user-guide.zh-CN.md:315 state it unconditionally.
findings.fix: Hedge the dma-buf sentence in the CHANGELOG and both user guides until a device run confirms it. For example: 'With GStreamer 1.24 or later, where the GPU driver imports the decoder's surfaces, a VA-API decoder's pictures are sampled in place (not yet tried on a device)'. Add the device figures and the docs/benchmarks record once measured.

findings.issue: The harness exercises only the GL ES 3 path. Mesa gives an ES 3.2 context for a client-version-2 request, so es3_, texture_rg_ and row_length_ are all true on llvmpipe. The shipped ES 2 fallbacks (LUMINANCE/LUMINANCE_ALPHA planes, padded rows with scaled coordinates, OES vertex arrays) and SavedState's restoration of Flutter's GL state are never tested. Both run in the real app, and both can be tested on llvmpipe in CI.
findings.evidence: VideoGl::ReadCaps (desktop_video_gl.cc:414-418) derives every fallback from the context version and extensions. Raster::Run builds `new pb_video::VideoGl(module_)` with no way to force them. No check sets non-default state (a bound FBO, a program, textures or samplers on units 0-2, scissor, blend, UNPACK_ROW_LENGTH, a pixel-unpack buffer, a VAO) before Convert and compares it afterwards. The implementer lists 'that populate leaves Skia and Impeller rendering intact' and 'the ES 2 fallbacks work' as device-only.
findings.fix: Give VideoGl a test-only constructor flag, or an environment knob read once at startup in the harness's own binary, that forces es3_, texture_rg_ and row_length_ false. Run the PSNR check a second time with it. Add a check that sets a known non-default GL state, calls Convert and ReadBack, and asserts that every saved binding and switch is back.

reviews.notes:
I compared every step of the brief with the diff 1515eda..5f42313; the implementation matches the corrected design.

**What matches the brief:**
- **Measurement commit first.** The module has `timings.decode`, and the harness reports per-thread CPU from schedstat/stat for the GStreamer threads and from getrusage(RUSAGE_THREAD) for the raster thread.
- **Module, ABI 2.** No videoconvert unless the decoder's templates cannot meet NV12/I420. DMA_DRM caps are requested only when the presenter imports dma-bufs and GStreamer is 1.24 or later. Candidates accept system memory or DMABuf. `create` takes the presenter. `describe` uses GstVideoMeta offsets, so 1088-row surfaces crop. `snapshot` uses GstVideoConverter. The allocation probe adds VideoMeta and asks for 3 held buffers.
- **GL helper in the runner.**
  - Planes are R8/RG8 or LUMINANCE, with ROW_LENGTH or padded rows; dma-buf planes become per-plane R8/GR88 EGLImages, cached by inode.
  - One pass uses Kr/Kb and the range from the caps. I checked the BT.709 coefficients and the U/V order for GR88 and RG.
  - Every binding and switch it touches is saved and restored.
  - Fence-gated release holds at most 2 pictures. GL_OES_EGL_image is checked at the first conversion; a failure refuses dma-bufs, falls back at the next keyframe and asks for one.
- **FlTextureGL.** The texture shows a 1x1 black before the first picture, a 320 px still at most once a second for dma-bufs, and stays JPEG under the software renderer.
- **Build and CI.** The runner links epoxy, which libgtk-3-dev brings, so release-ui.yml needs nothing new. The module links gstreamer-allocators, which libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev ships. The CI packages are valid jammy names.

**Things I checked that hold:**
- Flutter's EGL ES2 contexts (fl_opengl_manager.cc). `populate` runs on the raster thread with the render context current. Skia resets its own state before the callback; Impeller needs GL_RGBA8 (embedder_external_texture_gl.cc).
- No Xlib macro (None, Status, Bool and so on) clashes with identifiers in the changed C++.
- The GStreamer calls match the 1.20 headers.
- The harness checks would fail without the change: PSNR against the converter catches a flipped picture, swapped U/V or the wrong range; the RGBA8 and size check; I420 with no videoconvert.
- No figures appear in the docs, CHANGELOG or comments: the measurements are honestly absent.
- The English and Chinese user guides changed together. There is no Rust or Dart change, so snafu, testkit, environment-write, AppIcons and l10n rules do not apply.

**Not done (complete=false):**

The `stats` handler in desktop_video.cc will conflict, and so will PB_VIDEO_MODULE_ABI if that PR also moves it. Set the ABI to one above master's value at merge. The two commits f38f86a and 99283db both say ABI 2 with different structs; that is harmless if the PR is squashed.

Compiling against the real headers (clang for the app, GCC 11 -Wall -Werror for the harness), the surfaceless llvmpipe context, the PSNR threshold and check-linux-bundle.sh are left to CI's linux-app job.

name: direct-cooldown
title: Share the direct-fallback cooldown across connect_tcp calls per Client and service

commits: 7bc401f Share the direct-fallback cooldown across connect_tcp calls
e364903 Document the shared direct cooldown and record its measurement
impl.summary:
The pause after a direct fallback is now shared across connect_tcp calls. A Client and its carrier siblings keep the direct pause and the LAN-TCP pause per service, so a fallback in one connect_tcp sends the client's next calls to that service straight to the relay. Before, each call built a fresh Consumer and paid the punch budget again.

File by file (paths relative to /Users/lb7666/rust_pro/pb-mapper/.claude/worktrees/wf_43788853-efb-11):
- crates/pb-mapper-client/src/direct/memory.rs (new):
  - Cooldown and COOLDOWN_INITIAL/COOLDOWN_MAX moved here from consumer.rs unchanged, plus a `until()` accessor.
  - `Pauses` holds the direct Cooldown, the TCP Cooldown and the network generation they were learned on. `on_network(generation)` clears both when the generation differs.
  - A cfg(test)-only `block_quic` fault drops every QUIC packet a consumer's endpoint sends.
  - `SharedPauses = Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<Pauses>>`.
  - `DirectMemory` maps service to SharedPauses, at most MAX_SERVICES = 64 entries. When full, it first drops the entries that pause nothing now or were learned on another network generation, then the one whose pause ends soonest.
- crates/pb-mapper-client/src/direct/consumer.rs:
  - Consumer holds `pauses: SharedPauses`, passed to `Consumer::new` as a new last argument.
  - `cooldown()` and `tcp_cooldown()` lock the shared entry through `pauses()`, which first applies `on_network(remote.network_generation())`. So a network change clears the pause even for a consumer that no watcher wakes.
  - A skip because of another call's fallback now also reports `diagnostics.direct_cooldown(until)`, so the skipping connection's metrics show `direct_cooldown_ms`.
  - Back-off and clear-on-success work as before. `PUNCH_BUDGET` is pub(super) for the test. The test fault is applied where the consumer creates its Network.
- crates/pb-mapper-client/src/direct/mod.rs: declares `mod memory` and re-exports DirectMemory and SharedPauses to the crate.
- crates/pb-mapper-client/src/sdk/client.rs:
  - ClientInner gains `#[cfg(feature = "p2p")] direct_memory: Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<DirectMemory>>`, created in from_credential.
  - `with_relay_transport` siblings share it, as they share the credential.
  - connect_tcp passes it to run_owned_stream.
- crates/pb-mapper-client/src/client/mod.rs:
  - run_owned_stream takes the memory as a cfg(p2p) argument. When direct is on, it takes the service's entry, with the current network generation, and gives it to Consumer::new.

impl.deviations:
1. Key: DirectMemory is keyed by service key alone, not by (relay endpoint identity, namespace, service key). A memory belongs to one ClientInner and its with_relay_transport siblings. They share it, as they share the credential, and they all have the same relay name and namespace, both fixed at construction; root rotation only swaps one administrator key for another. Adding relay and namespace to the key would store constant data. The intent, that entries never mix relays or namespaces, holds because each Client has its own memory.

2. Generation: Pauses keeps the generation it was last brought to. Every read or write first brings it to the current generation and clears both pauses if it differs. A back-off is therefore always recorded under the generation that is current when it happens, which is what "the generation of its last back-off" asks for. Listener consumers read through the same check. It is equivalent to the `invalidate()` they already get on Wake::Network, which is kept.

3. Diagnostics: a cooldown skip now also reports `direct_cooldown(until)`. A connect_tcp that skips because of an earlier call's fallback would otherwise show `cooldown_skips` 1 with no `direct_cooldown_ms`. For listener tunnels the value is the same `until` they already reported.

4. Test fault: the cfg(test) fault (`block_quic`) is carried on the shared Pauses entry. That is the only path from a test's Client into the Consumer that connect_tcp builds internally.

5. Step 4 of the design (sharing the consumer Network per entry with a 60 s idle expiry) was not built. The design makes it conditional on device SetupTimings showing at least 100 ms of discovery plus mapping per connect, and that data does not exist yet.

6. User guide: docs/user-guide.md and docs/user-guide.zh-CN.md were not changed. Their fallback paragraph describes connect tunnels, which are unchanged; the viewer-facing change is in remote-desktop.md and the CHANGELOG.

7. Timing slack: the brief's timing assertion is implemented literally. Across five release runs and one debug run, the slack over PUNCH_BUDGET was 18–46 ms. The first call also pays negotiation (a status query, a control connection, generating a certificate, STUN and the grant) on top of the punch, so the margin comes from the code's structure, not luck. A very loaded CI runner is the only flake risk I can see.

findings.issue: The shared pause is also set by a connect_tcp that fails outright: the publisher is not registered (host rebooting, or its app restarting) or the relay cannot be reached. That pause now outlives the failed call. The client's next connect_tcp to that computer skips direct, and because a connect_tcp stream is never upgraded, the viewer session that finally reconnects stays on the relay for its whole life, even though a punch would have worked. Each failed retry after a pause expires doubles the pause (10 s, 20 s, 40 s and so on, up to 5 min), so a host restart longer than one pause makes it likely. Before this PR the pause ended with each call's own Consumer, so the reconnect after the host returned tried direct again. These are the exact cases the desktop reconnect loop (1, 2, 4, 8, 15 s) exists for, and remote-desktop.md's claim that only 'a path that cannot be punched' goes to the relay does not hold for them.
findings.evidence:
Code path: Client::connect_tcp -> TunnelWorker::prepare (does not contact the relay) -> run_owned_stream takes the client's shared entry -> handle_local_stream calls direct.prepare first. With the publisher absent, negotiate returns Ok(None) (FallbackReason::NotOffered, line 279). With the relay unreachable, control() fails (NegotiationFailed). Either way self.back_off() runs before the relay subscription, which then fails too.
Two temporary probe tests in direct/tests.rs, run here and then reverted:
(a) TestRelay offering direct, no publisher. connect_tcp("host") failed after 8.0 s with fallbacks 1, last_fallback "direct_not_offered". I then registered the publisher with allow_direct. The same client's next connect_tcp printed `cooldown_skips 1, (direct_sessions, relay_sessions) = (0, 1)`. A fresh Client to the same publisher printed `cooldown_skips 0, (1, 0)`, so direct worked.
(b) Relay port closed. Round 0 printed `ready ok=false after 8.0s; fallbacks 1, cooldown_skips 0, direct paused afterwards true`. Round 1 printed `ready ok=false ...; fallbacks 0, cooldown_skips 1`.
memory.rs Cooldown::back_off arms a new, doubled pause whenever none is running.
findings.fix:
Keep a pause in the shared entry only when the relay path then proves the publisher is there:
- For NotOffered, NegotiationFailed and NegotiationTimeout, have prepare return the relay decision without arming the pause. handle_local_stream then calls a new Consumer method (for example `fell_back()`, which runs back_off) only after subscription.with_retry succeeds.
- In the Unreachable branch, call back_off after self.relay(...) has subscribed, not before it.
- A setup that fails altogether leaves the entry unchanged.
Add a test like probe (a): a connect_tcp with no publisher fails; after register_with_options(allow_direct) the client's next connect_tcp goes direct (cooldown_skips 0, direct_sessions 1). Note in remote-desktop.md that a session which takes the relay stays on it.

findings.issue: The timing assertion `skipped + PUNCH_BUDGET <= fell_back` has a margin of only a couple of tens of milliseconds. The margin is the first call's extra work (status query, control connection, certificate, STUN, grant, DirectRelay) minus the second call's plain relay setup. On its own, the second call varied from 6.7 ms to 25.5 ms across runs here, which is about as large as the margin. A pause on the second call alone, for example on a busy ubuntu-latest runner during `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, fails the gate. The cooldown_skips and fallbacks counters already prove that direct was skipped.
findings.evidence: 8 quiet debug runs here (fell_back - 2 s - skipped): 26.3, 23.9, 23.4, 24.8, 20.7, 24.6, 352.7 and 22.8 ms. In 10 runs with 10 copies of the lib suite running at once, `skipped` reached 25.5 ms. The implementer reports 18-46 ms of slack across 6 runs.
findings.fix: Keep the counter assertions. Replace the timing check with one that tolerates jitter but still shows the punch budget was not spent, for example `assert!(fell_back >= PUNCH_BUDGET && skipped < PUNCH_BUDGET / 4)`. Or compare with tolerance: `skipped + PUNCH_BUDGET / 2 <= fell_back`.

findings.issue:
The shared pause also learns from fallbacks that say nothing about the path. For a remote desktop viewer, each connect_tcp is a whole session that can never move to direct later. So a reconnect made while the host was briefly unregistered, or while the relay was down, gets every later session to that computer put on the relay for its whole life, even after direct works again. Before this branch, each viewer connect started with a fresh Consumer and tried direct again.

The cases:
- The host is away (restarting, or re-registering after a network change) or its registration is unhealthy. The relay answers the grant with LegacyRelay (pb-mapper-server/src/direct/state.rs: no healthy registration that allows direct), which becomes `Ok(None)` and then FallbackReason::NotOffered, and `self.back_off()` (line 279) writes to the shared entry.

While the outage lasts, every attempt that finds the pause expired backs off again: 10 s, 20 s, 40 s, up to 5 min. The app's reconnects at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 15 s therefore keep landing inside a growing pause. The brief accepted only that a direct path 'waits out the cooldown (10 s at first)'. **The brief, step by step**
- Step 1 is built. `ClientInner.direct_memory` is `Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<DirectMemory>>` and holds at most 64 entries. Idle or stale-generation entries go first, then the one whose pause ends soonest. Each entry holds the direct Cooldown, the TCP Cooldown and a generation. `with_relay_transport` siblings and clones share it.
  - Keying by service alone is justified. The memory is per Client, the namespace is fixed when the Client is built, and root rotation only goes from admin to admin (admin/mod.rs:331-355).
  - Both carriers' RelayEndpoints use `NetworkHints::shared()`, so siblings read the same generation and the clearing cannot flip-flop between them.
- Step 2 is built. `cooldown()` and `tcp_cooldown()` go through `on_network(remote.network_generation())`. A success still clears the pause. A skip now also reports `direct_cooldown`.
  - No lock is held across an await or held twice. The DirectMemory lock is always taken before the Pauses lock, never the reverse.
- Step 3 holds. Each listener gets a private SharedPauses, and its behaviour is equivalent to before.
- Step 4 (sharing the consumer Network) was deferred with a valid reason: it depends on SetupTimings from devices.
- Step 5 (docs and CHANGELOG) is done.
  - remote-desktop.md, architecture.md and crates/pb-mapper/README.md have no Chinese pair, so the doc pairs are consistent. Leaving user-guide.md and user-guide.zh-CN.md unchanged is reasonable.
  - The change also makes remote-desktop.md:645 true for the viewer ("the viewer stops asking for a while"). Before this branch that was false, because each connect_tcp started with a fresh TCP pause.

**Will users see the effect?** Yes, for unpunchable paths.
- The app's viewer calls `Viewer::connect`, which calls `client.connect_tcp` on the FFI's cached `relay_client()`. That client is kept while `same_relay` holds, so the pause carries across reconnects on Windows, macOS and Linux viewers.

impl.summary:
The branch starts at 1515eda. Changes by file:
- crates/pb-mapper-server/src/tcp_tuning.rs (new):
  - `TcpCongestion` is a checked name: 1 to 15 ASCII letters, digits, `_` or `-`. Linux's TCP_CA_NAME_MAX is 16, and the kernel quietly cuts a longer name short. It implements FromStr and Display. A bad name gives `InvalidTcpCongestion` (snafu).

impl.deviations:
1. Where the congestion control is set. The brief says to set TCP_CONGESTION on each accepted socket in connection.rs:117-121. I set it once on the listening socket instead. Linux hands a congestion control chosen by setsockopt on a listener to every connection it accepts: the clone copies the choice and tcp_ca_openreq_child keeps it when icsk_ca_setsockopt is set, and tcp_reinit_congestion_control explicitly handles the TCPF_LISTEN state. So every accepted relay socket still gets the algorithm, with these differences:
   - The accept loop does no work per connection.
   - A refusal (ENOENT or EPERM) shows up once, at startup, which is the brief's "log once", without a per-connection flag.
   - connection.rs is untouched.
   - A Linux-only test (`accepted_connections_take_the_listeners_congestion_control`) pins the inheritance. It runs only in CI.
2. No field on RelayServerOptions. The brief asks to add the option "to RelayServerOptions following its existing pattern without breaking public struct literals", and both cannot hold. Any new public field breaks existing literals such as `RelayServerOptions { direct, quic }`, which the crate README and the FFI use. Because the setting now lives on the listener, the public API instead gains `pb_mapper_server::set_tcp_congestion(&listener, &TcpCongestion)`. The CLI calls it on the listener it already binds before handing it to `run_server_on_listener_with_options`, and existing literals keep compiling. The cost: the app's built-in relay (FFI) and the `run_server*` entry points that bind their own listener cannot opt in. The brief only asked for the CLI and Docker.
3. Where things are logged. The idle-restart notice is logged by the server library at relay startup, so any embedder on Linux also logs it. The congestion outcome is logged by the CLI from the typed error.
4. Additions beyond the brief:
   - `PB_MAPPER_TCP_TUNING=yes|no` to answer the installer prompt without a terminal.
   - An invalid `PB_MAPPER_TCP_CONGESTION` fails at startup, like the other server flag checks. A blank value counts as unset.
5. Left out of the docs: the research item's suggested remark that kernel BBR is "BBRv1/v3 with a decaying bandwidth filter, unlike the quinn fork's". I could not verify which BBR version the mainline kernel ships, and it is not part of the brief's design.
6. Measurements: none. See below.

findings.issue: In the Docker setup this PR documents, a refused `--tcp-congestion` / `PB_MAPPER_TCP_CONGESTION` produces no log at all, and refusal is the normal Docker result. Both docker/docker-compose.yml (line 12) and both DOCKER_README examples (lines 18 and 31) set `RUST_LOG=error`. The refusal `relay_tcp_congestion_unavailable` is logged at warn, and the success event `relay_tcp_congestion` and the `relay_tcp_idle_restart` notice at info, so that filter drops all three. A container has no CAP_NET_ADMIN by default, and a stock host allows only `reno cubic` in tcp_allowed_congestion_control. Uncommenting `PB_MAPPER_TCP_CONGESTION: bbr` therefore usually gets EPERM, or ENOENT when tcp_bbr is not loaded, and nothing is shown. The operator cannot tell whether BBR took effect. That defeats the brief's "on EPERM or ENOENT log once with the fix" on the main deployment path. DOCKER_README line 101 and docs/user-guide.md line 293 also promise the log unconditionally.
findings.evidence: Ran here: `RUST_LOG=error target/debug/pb-mapper server --port 47691 --relay-only --auth-state-dir <scratch> --init-admin-key --force-init-admin-key --tcp-congestion bbr` printed only the admin-key line. The same command with `RUST_LOG=warn` printed `WARN ... relay_tcp_congestion_unavailable ... fix: only a relay on Linux can choose its TCP congestion control` (at server.rs:199). docker-compose.yml:12 sets `RUST_LOG: error`, and :17 is the commented `# PB_MAPPER_TCP_CONGESTION: bbr`. DOCKER_README.md:101 says "When the kernel refuses, the relay logs `relay_tcp_congestion_unavailable` with the fix". Kernel tcp_set_congestion_control returns -EPERM when !(ca->flags & TCP_CONG_NON_RESTRICTED) && !cap_net_admin. tcp_ca_find_autoload loads a module only when capable(CAP_NET_ADMIN).

Alternatively write it to stderr regardless of the filter, as `administrator key initialized` is. Consider the same for the success event so the operator can confirm it. Also, in the commented line in docker-compose.yml and in DOCKER_README's TCP tuning section, say that the outcome is logged at warn/info (or error, after the change) and how to check it, e.g. `docker exec pb-mapper cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_allowed_congestion_control` or `ss -ti`.

Reviewed `git diff 1515eda..perf2/relay-tcp-tuning` with HEAD detached at 139c991; the worktree is still clean.

**Checked and correct**
- **socket2 0.6.1 calls.** `set_tcp_congestion(&[u8])` and `tcp_congestion() -> Vec<u8>` are methods on `Socket`, reached through `SockRef`'s `Deref`. Both are behind `cfg(all(feature = "all", linux or freebsd))`, and `TCP_CA_NAME_MAX = 16`. tokio's TcpListener and TcpStream implement `AsFd`. libc 0.2.190 defines `TCP_CONGESTION` for every linux_like target, musl included. Android and Windows take the non-Linux path, and the socket2 dependency is gated to Linux.
- **Kernel behaviour.** Setting the algorithm on a listening socket and having accepted sockets inherit it is sound. `tcp_reinit_congestion_control` sets `icsk_ca_setsockopt` and skips init in the LISTEN state. `tcp_ca_openreq_child` keeps the listener's algorithm unless a route's `congctl` overrides it. The 15-byte name limit is correct: the kernel's `strncpy_from_sockptr` copies at most `TCP_CA_NAME_MAX - 1` bytes. ENOENT and EPERM map to the right fixes, and tcp_allowed_congestion_control is not namespaced, as the code says.
- **Deviations.** The listener-level setting instead of a per-socket one, and the absent `RelayServerOptions` field, are justified: a new public field would break existing literals such as testkit's `RelayServerOptions { direct, quic: None }`. The cost is that the FFI's built-in relay cannot opt in, which the brief did not require.

  - `cargo test -p pb-mapper-cli --bin pb-mapper server::`: 5 passed.

findings.issue: In the shipped Docker setup, the relay says nothing when it refuses the congestion control. docker/docker-compose.yml:12 and both DOCKER_README examples set RUST_LOG=error. `relay_tcp_congestion_unavailable` is logged at warn and the success event `relay_tcp_congestion` at info, so both are filtered out. An operator who uncomments `# PB_MAPPER_TCP_CONGESTION: bbr` (compose line 17) without preparing the host keeps Cubic and gets no log line. Docker's defaults make this the usual case: containers have no NET_ADMIN, and the allowed list is normally `reno cubic`, so the kernel returns EPERM. DOCKER_README and both user-guide pages still say the relay "logs relay_tcp_congestion_unavailable with the fix". The design's "log once with the fix" never reaches this deployment's operator.
findings.evidence: I ran it here with `PB_MAPPER_TCP_CONGESTION=bbr ./target/debug/pb-mapper server --port 47913 --relay-only --auth-state-dir <scratch>`. With RUST_LOG=error it printed nothing. With RUST_LOG=warn it printed `WARN ... event="relay_tcp_congestion_unavailable" congestion=bbr error=unsupported fix=...`. logging.rs builds its filter with `EnvFilter ... from_env_lossy()`, so RUST_LOG=error drops warn and info.
findings.fix: The operator asked for this explicitly, so log the refusal at `error` level, or also print it with eprintln! as `--init-admin-key` does. Otherwise, say in the compose comment and DOCKER_README's TCP tuning section that RUST_LOG must be `warn` or lower to see the outcome.

findings.issue: Before this change the installer never read input. Its new prompt reads /dev/tty with no timeout, so a run that has a controlling terminal but nobody at it now waits forever, partway through the install. Examples are `ssh -t host 'curl ... | sudo bash'` from a script, or a provisioning tool that allocates a pty. The same line is in install-server-gitee.sh:144. The comment's "Asked only on a terminal, once" is also wrong: an answer of no writes nothing, so every reinstall asks again.
findings.evidence: `git show 1515eda:scripts/install-server-github.sh | grep 'read \|/dev/tty'` finds nothing. I ran the extracted step under a pty whose input stays open but empty: `sleep 8 | script -q /dev/null bash step.sh` (scratchpad review-tcp-installer/run.sh). It printed the [y/N] prompt and was still waiting after 4 s.
findings.fix: Use `read -r -t 60 TCP_TUNING </dev/tty || TCP_TUNING=""` in both scripts, so a timeout counts as no, and print a newline after it times out. Change the comment to say it asks again on a later run unless PB_MAPPER_TCP_TUNING answers.

findings.issue: The TCP tuning section and the compose comment say both settings act on "what the relay sends ... to the viewer". That holds only when the viewer's TCP connection ends inside the container's network namespace, as with bridge networking and iptables DNAT. When a user-space proxy carries the published port, the long leg to the viewer is the proxy's socket in the host namespace. That socket uses the host's tcp_slow_start_after_idle and default congestion control, so the container sysctl and --tcp-congestion change only the short veth hop. The proxy cases are docker-proxy for IPv6 publishing without ip6tables (the default before Docker 27), and the port drivers of rootless Docker (RootlessKit) and rootless Podman (rootlessport). The README itself recommends `"[::]:7666:7666/tcp"` publishing with USE_IPV6 (line 76).
findings.evidence: This is how Docker is built: docker-proxy and the rootless port drivers accept the client's TCP connection in the host namespace and open a second one to the container, which is why the container sees the proxy's or gateway's address as the source. The diff changes only the container's namespace (`sysctls`) and the relay's own listener (`set_tcp_congestion`).
findings.fix: Add one sentence to DOCKER_README's TCP tuning section and the compose comment. It should say that both settings apply to connections the relay itself terminates. Where docker-proxy or a rootless port driver carries the port (IPv6 publishing without ip6tables, rootless Docker or Podman), the host's own settings apply instead: set net.ipv4.tcp_slow_start_after_idle (and, if wanted, net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_control) on the host.

findings.issue: The guide says "A relay that runs as root, as the install scripts' service does, may then choose it". It never says how to give that service the option, and neither user-guide page mentions /etc/pb-mapper/server.env. The install scripts write a unit with a fixed `ExecStart=... pb-mapper server --port ${PORT}`, so the installed relay picks up PB_MAPPER_TCP_CONGESTION only through `EnvironmentFile=-/etc/pb-mapper/server.env`. That unit is the deployment where BBR works with no extra steps (root with CAP_NET_ADMIN, so the module autoloads), yet its operators get no instructions. The Chinese page has the same gap at docs/user-guide.zh-CN.md:187.

DOCKER_README also gives an nsenter + `ss -ti` command that shows each relay connection's algorithm, and says the examples' RUST_LOG=error hides the info-level relay_tcp_idle_restart.

A malformed PB_MAPPER_TCP_CONGESTION stopped the relay (confirmed: the relay's other env settings, such as legacy_protocol_from_env and env_usize/env_u64, log and fall back). tcp_congestion_from_env now returns Option. An invalid or non-UTF-8 value logs error event relay_tcp_congestion_invalid and returns None, so the relay starts with the system default. The ServerFlagError::TcpCongestionEnv variant is gone, and --tcp-congestion stays strict through clap. The unit test now asserts None for 'bbr cubic'. A run here with PB_MAPPER_TCP_CONGESTION='bbr cubic' logged the error, served, and exited 0 on SIGINT. CHANGELOG and both user guides say an invalid value is logged and ignored.

Installer prompt hang (confirmed: `read` from /dev/tty with no timeout). Both install scripts, still identical apart from DOWNLOAD_URL, now use `read -r -t 60`: a timeout or EOF counts as no and prints a newline. The prompt is also skipped while /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_slow_start_after_idle already reads 0. The comment no longer says 'once': a later run asks again after a no. The message after a failed `sysctl -w` no longer promises the setting at the next boot: it says it applies then if this kernel allows it.

User-space proxy caveat (correct: docker-proxy for IPv6 publishing without ip6tables, and rootless Docker/Podman port drivers, end the viewer's TCP connection in the host namespace). DOCKER_README's TCP tuning section, the compose sysctls comment and the CHANGELOG now say that in those setups the host's own net.ipv4.tcp_slow_start_after_idle (and net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_control for BBR) apply.

Missing service instructions (confirmed: the installer's unit and services/pb-mapper-server.service read EnvironmentFile=-/etc/pb-mapper/server.env, and neither user guide mentioned it). Both user-guide pages, kept in step, now give the commands: mkdir -p /etc/pb-mapper, append PB_MAPPER_TCP_CONGESTION=bbr to server.env, then restart pb-mapper-server. They note that a root relay may choose any algorithm its kernel ships and the kernel loads the module itself. services/readme.md has one matching sentence.
Reviewer observation, also fixed: the docs now say 'every TCP connection the relay accepts', because QUIC relay connections under --quic-listen are not covered.
